messages:
Maya (Marketing): Hey team — we need a quick latency + cost audit for the assets we're using in the launch post and webinar. Target: p95/p99 token latency, 1k-token cost estimates, and a small smoke run we can quote in marketing materials. Deadline: EOD Tuesday.

Maya (Marketing): Scope: hosted API + dedicated variant, models: redwood-v3-base, redwood-v3-large, and a quantized pick (redwood-v3-large-8bit). Also one external baseline (llama2-13b) if easy.

Leo (Eng Runtime): Got it. Quick clarifying Qs: do you want long-context patterns (4k tokens) or mostly short chat turns? Also which hardware configs for Dedicated? A10G only or H100 too?

Maya (Marketing): Primarily short chat (avg 60 tokens) for live demo numbers, and a few long-context samples (2 samples at ~2000 tokens) for the deep-dive slide. Dedicated: H100 preferred if available; fallback A10G is fine.

Sam (Eng Runtime): I can run a small smoke sweep tomorrow morning. Plan: 50 short prompts x 3 concurrency levels (1, 8, 32) + 2 long prompts single-concurrency. Collect per-request total latency, server-side token emission latency, and token counts. Output CSV + simple aggregate summary (p50/p95/p99).

Sam (Eng Runtime): Suggested payload (curl for hosted API):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v3-large","input":"Summarize: Why inference performance matters for developers","max_tokens":200}'
```

Jordan (DevEx): FYI we have a bench-runner job template (go/redwood/bench-runbook) that already collects token-level traces + system metrics (CPU/GPU util, mem). If you want consistent numbers for the launch, use that template and tag runs with `marketing-launch-2026` so we can reproduce later.

Maya (Marketing): Perfect — please use the bench-runner template. Important: include raw CSV and a 1-slide summary for the press kit with 3 bullets (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, fallback notes). Also call out any surprising variance or QoS regressions.

Leo (Eng Runtime): One more: do you want warm-cache (prefix cache) numbers or cold-cache? Both would be ideal but if we must choose, give me priority order.

Maya (Marketing): Both. Warm-cache is primary for customer-facing numbers; include cold-cache as a footnote.

Sam (Eng Runtime): Ok scheduling: I'll queue small runs tonight on hosted and dedicated staging. If perf-bot can start jobs, great — otherwise I'll trigger manually. Expect preliminary CSVs + slide by 2026-03-30 10:00 PT.

perf-bot: Job queued: bench-runner/marketing-launch-2026 on runner-staging-3 (H100). Job id: br-54231.

Leo (Eng Runtime): If we hit unexpected tail latencies I'll capture full traces and the model kv-cache stats. Heads-up: quantized 8bit variants sometimes change token throughput numbers ~10-25%.

Maya (Marketing): Noted. If quantized runs look better on cost with <10% quality delta, we may call that out.

Jordan (DevEx): Linking runbook: https://go.redwood/bench-runbook — please add the command you ran to the bench-run job notes. Also include the exact docker image + git sha for reproducibility.

Sam (Eng Runtime): Will do. Quick plan summary: 1) small hosted smoke (short prompts) 2) dedicated H100 run (short + long) 3) quantized variant run (short) 4) aggregate CSV + 1-slide.

Maya (Marketing): Thank you — please ping me once the slide is ready so we can prep the PR/launch language. :thumbsup:

Leo (Eng Runtime): Ping me if any capacity or infra blockers come up.

Sam (Eng Runtime): will ping here. Starting now.
